text:
maya: heads up — we started seeing a sharp uptick in admission rejections originating from eu-west1 around 10:04 UTC, small-model traffic. Clients are reporting 503 + Retry-After instead of the usual 429 :warning:
harper: can you paste an example response? is the gateway toggling a policy? :thinking:
maya: snippet from edge logs:
```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2026 10:04:12 GMT
X-RI-Est-Delay: 120
Retry-After: 120
Content-Type: application/json

{ "error": "execution_unavailable", "detail": "region saturated, queued requests suspended" }
```
linus: 503 semantics here are important — 429 implies client exceeded a rate, 503 says infra can't handle it. Our SDKs historically treated 503 as retryable without token/backoff adjustments, which created retry storms when region recovered :ambulance:
harper: i think the recent admission-controller change swapped from immediate 429 rejects to soft-queueing + 503 when queue depth > 200 to avoid dropping requests. the idea was to preserve client work, but it backfired with aggressive SDK retries.
ops-bot: deploy-canary: admission-controller v2.4.1 toggled eu-west1 soft-queue-mode ON at 2026-11-04T10:00:00Z :gear:
maya: right — we got the canary on eu-west and traffic pattern amplified. clients that don't honor X-RI-Est-Delay or that do fixed millisecond backoff kept hammering the queue. we need guidance for SDKs and short-term mitigation.
linus: mitigation options:
- flip soft-queue off (back to 429) temporarily
- emit capacity tokens in the handshake so clients can do polite rate limiting
- enrich Retry-After with ms precision and a max-backoff header
- add a `X-RI-Queue-Pos` header so friendly SDKs can jitter based on position

harper: i'd add a cost note — queued requests currently reserve memory/kv cache slots and may bill against committed throughput in Dedicated. longer queues -> higher unit cost for customers. customers will be unhappy if we silently queue then bill.
devx: for SDK changes we can push a micro-release with client behavior:
```
// pseudo
if (status == 503) {
  let serverDelay = getHeader('Retry-After-ms') || getHeader('Retry-After') * 1000 || 2000;
  // server tells us expected window; apply capped exponential backoff + server jitter
  let wait = min(maxBackoffMs, exponentialBackoff(base=200, attempt) + random(-0.2,0.2)*serverDelay);
  scheduleRetry(wait);
}
```
devx: also add logic to stop retries after totalRetryBudgetMs exceeded and surface a clear error to app layer to avoid infinite retries.
sre-oncall: short-term: i'm going to flip eu-west1 soft-queue-mode -> false for 10m while we confirm SDK changes and capacity tokens. flipping will return to 429 semantics so well-behaved SDKs back off sooner. notifying pagerduty.
ops-bot: action: toggle soft-queue eu-west1 OFF scheduled at 2026-11-04T10:12:00Z by @sre-oncall
maya: thanks — also can we add telemetry: `infra.admit_mode` and `client.retry_storm_rate` metrics to alert quickly if a region is in soft-queue and retries spike? would help detect this faster.
linus: agree. longer term roadmap items:
- admission token handshake: clients request a short-lived admit token in create-stream; controller returns token_count & refill_rate headers so SDKs can implement local leaky-bucket before hitting network. header names: `X-RI-Admit-Token`, `X-RI-Token-Refill-ms`
- support `202 Accepted` + queue handle instead of 503 so clients can poll with exponential backoff rather than immediate retrying
- opt-in billing flag for queued requests so customers can choose immediate reject vs queued billing

harper: for release notes we should call out the behavior change for canary and our recommended SDK bump. i'll draft a short note for ops-runbook and customers.
maya: ok — i'll coordinate with devx to push SDK patch, sre-oncall will flip canary now, ops-bot will run the toggle action, and linus will start work on token handshake design. thanks all :wave:
